source_title: SigmaRoc Annual Report and Financial Statements 2019
availability_evidence: Annual report pages 18 and 28 state that the report and financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 17 April 2020; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 70.6% to £70.4m, underlying EBITDA 47.6% to £14.5m and underlying profit before tax 51.3% to £8.4m, while underlying EBITDA margin remained strong at 20.7%. Acquisition activity lifted adjusted leverage to 2.07x and net debt to £49.8m, operating cash generation fell to £2.1m from £5.5m and refinancing remained in progress, although covenants were comfortably met. The April 2020 report described significant Covid uncertainty but stress-tested liquidity and retained a going-concern conclusion.
already_announced_exclusion: The Aberdo quarry turnaround, subsidiary rebranding and alignment, Bury-site discontinuation, announced acquisition integrations and Covid contingency actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Covid uncertainty, weaker operating cash generation, acquisition-funded debt growth and pending refinancing create moderate pressure. Very strong revenue and EBITDA growth, resilient margins, covenant compliance and substantial asset backing provide strong contrary evidence.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 42 and 69 state that the report and financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 22 March 2022; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 118.9% to £272.0m, underlying EBITDA 106.1% to £49.3m and underlying EPS 19.4%, with like-for-like growth and profitability protected despite energy, logistics and input-cost inflation. Net debt rose to £164.0m after the Nordkalk-led acquisition programme, but leverage was 1.88x against a 3.5x covenant, cash was £70m, undrawn facilities about £200m and cash generated from operations increased to £29.5m. The outlook remained positive despite early-2022 disruption.
already_announced_exclusion: The Nordkalk, B-Mix and Casters integrations, completed management and reporting changes, subsidiary rebranding and alignment, announced efficiency initiatives, refinancing and other acquisition actions disclosed before cutoff are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Inflation and supply-chain headwinds plus substantially higher acquisition debt create limited pressure. Exceptional growth, resilient margins, higher operating cash, low leverage relative to covenants and extensive liquidity provide very strong offsets.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 141 and 198 state that the report and financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 17 March 2024; issuer-linked report-viewer PDF bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 8% to £580.3m, underlying EBITDA 15% to £116.7m and underlying EBITDA margin 120bps to 20.1%, despite a 4% like-for-like volume decline and difficult residential markets. Net debt fell 6% to £182.4m and covenant leverage improved from 1.93x to 1.57x. Free cash flow remained solid at £47.0m but fell 12.7%, cash generated from operations declined to £65.4m and statutory profit and EPS were reduced by acquisition and reorganisation costs.
already_announced_exclusion: The six completed 2023 acquisitions and integrations, CRH Lime acquisitions announced in November 2023, disclosed site and operation discontinuations, redundancies, reorganisation programmes, refinancing and £4m annualised efficiency gains are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Softer volumes and cash generation, higher finance costs and difficult residential markets create limited pressure. Record underlying earnings, margin expansion, lower debt and leverage, positive free cash flow and strong pricing power provide exceptionally strong contrary evidence.
